description.narrative: (Lebanon): Using FY 2024 funds, USAID will continue to support the agri-food sector and other light industries to strengthen food security and improve livelihoods, sustain existing jobs while creating new ones, and increase farmers' and workers' incomes. ARE activity partners with micro, small, and medium enterprises to provide technical and financial resources to increase their competitiveness using a market systems approach, i.e., analyzing the actions and relationships among all input suppliers, farmers, businesspeople, and end-consumers for a given agricultural line of products. These "value chains" include fresh and processed produce, dairy and fodder, and fruit trees, to access domestic and export markets. The Mission is exploring how its ARE interventions can address the needs in the South and the Beqaa as a result of fighting between Hizballah and Israel. ARE will continue introducing cost-efficient interventions such as vegetable greenhouse upgrades with controlled atmospheric measures and new irrigation technologies. These practices not only increase crop production; they also reduce the use of chemicals and water. USAID will scale up interventions that ARE is developing using $5 million in FY 2024 Ukraine supplemental funds and launch new interventions to address food insecurity and support livelihoods through access to inputs, import substitution, reducing production and processing costs, and ensuring job creation or retention to increase or maintain household income. ARE's commitment to inclusive economic growth and improve employment opportunities, helps to pave Lebanon's path to long-term stability. Additionally, ARE will utilize $1.5 million in the Higher Education Economic Crises Directive (HEED) funds to partner with AUB's Advancing Research Enabling Communities Center to advance research and development for resilient crop varieties and more efficient technology adoption to improve productivity and food security.
